approvalScope: Only the visible pixels of the eight exact display-report screenshots, opened once each
summary: The complete-course overviews, initial viewports and two figure captures on desktop and mobile show no apparent overlap, clipping or blank media. Figure 54's apparatus/isotherm and Figure 55's English-compatible endpoint/temperature composition remain visually intelligible at the reported 640px and 358px media widths. English captions are identifiable and separated from surrounding content in the whole-page views. Tall-image downscaling limits fine-glyph and full-resolution certification; this is not headed, production, all-English accessibility or new source/geometry approval.

images.observation: The full desktop course has a consistent centered prose column, a readable English subject heading, unobstructed paragraph groups and both diagrams. The two concept separators do not collide with text. Figure 54 and Figure 55 captions are visibly below their respective figures and remain identifiable. The final warmer-curve explanation and diagram are present with bottom whitespace, not truncated. This whole-image overview was automatically downscaled.

Actual pixels show the N38 initial viewport, despite the inherited filename. The subject title and Chapter 4/printed-page breadcrumb are distinct; the motivation, fixed-total-mass experiment and work/heat text wrap within the column. Line and paragraph spacing prevent collisions. There is ordinary text continuation at the viewport bottom, not a missing or clipped media object.

The p-V isotherm, A-B plateau, dashed state projections and four cylinders/pistons/rods are clearly visible. Vapor dots, a shallow liquid layer in the mixture and the final liquid region are distinguishable. The labels and outer rods have clearance from the image edges and each other; no blank media or apparent clipping is present. The caption is not part of this figure-only capture.

Five visible curves, three finite plateaus, the critical K, dashed envelope and guides form an intact composition. V1/V1-prime remain on the liquid-left side, and V2-prime/V2 on the vapor-right side, consistent with the already-reviewed English explanation. The two tiers of volume labels and the temperature labels are distinguishable and unoccluded. No new source relationship or numeric reading is inferred.

The full mobile page preserves a single column, wrapped paragraphs, both figures, both captions and the final lesson content. The saturated-vapor definition is visibly emphasized after its separator, and the prime explanation/comparison remains above Figure 55. Captions are identifiable and separated, though small in the downscaled overview. No gross text collision, edge truncation or blank media is apparent; fine-glyph/full-resolution certification is excluded.

The N38 title fits within the 390px viewport; the breadcrumb wraps into two clean lines. Introductory English prose and the Figure 54 reference are readable within the margins, without heading or paragraph overlap. The content continues normally past the lower viewport edge. No claim is made that this headless capture is a headed product session.

At the reported 358px media width, p/V, origin, A/B and endpoint labels remain distinguishable. The graph and all four apparatus states, including their rightward rods and liquid/vapor distinctions, fit with visible margins. No apparent overlap, missing media or clipped rod/axis is present. Caption inspection comes from the whole-page view, not this capture.

The mobile curve family, finite plateaus, K, dashed envelope and guides are nonblank and contained. The tiered primed-volume labels and temperature labels remain distinguishable with no apparent collision. The visible liquid-left/vapor-right convention remains compatible with the English comparison. This is visible composition/context assessment, not renewed source-pixel or geometry approval.
